title: Don’t End TPS for Our Immigrant Neighbors
author: Jordan Liz
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2021/06/IMG_5463-680x510.jpeg)

Photograph by Nathaniel St. Clair

_This February, a panel of conservative[federal judges
ruled](https://www.sfchronicle.com/politics/article/9th-circuit-tps-
honduras-21343987.php) that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) can move
forward with terminating Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for immigrants from
Nicaragua, Honduras, and Nepal._

For the over 60,000 immigrants impacted by this decision, this is an
incredible loss. As [Jessica
Bansal](https://www.nationaltpsalliance.org/breaking-ninth-circuit-court-of-
appeals-permits-tps-terminations-for-honduras-nepal-and-nicaragua-to-take-
effec/), an attorney with the National Day Laborer Organizing Network, writes,
the “decision allows mothers, fathers, students, and workers who have lived
lawfully in this country for decades to be stripped of status without even
acknowledging the devastation caused to them and their families or the
contribution they have made to their communities.”

Let’s be clear about what’s happening here: DHS is eliminating
[TPS](https://www.americanimmigrationcouncil.org/blog/temporary-protected-
status-whats-up-with-that/) for immigrants who are lawfully residing in the
United States solely on the basis of their race, ethnicity, and nationality.
They are turning documented immigrants  _into_ undocumented immigrants,
slandering them as
“[killers](https://x.com/Sec_Noem/status/1995642101779124476)” and “leeches”
simply to create the pretext for more ICE violence.

This is not speculation. Before a judge blocked its termination, [TPS for
Haitians](https://media.wbur.org/wp/2026/02/Reyes-Opinion-TPS-Haiti.pdf) was
slated to end on February 3. News outlets began reporting in late January that
[the Trump administration](https://www.ms.now/news/ohio-ice-immigration-
operations-haitians-tps-noem) was planning to launch an operation targeting
Haitians in Springfield, Ohio and across the state.

The end of TPS would have set the stage for another brutal Minnesota-style
operation.

While [DHS](https://www.wosu.org/2026-02-10/dhs-claims-no-specific-plans-for-
springfield-ice-surge-if-tps-for-haitian-had-expired-feb-3) denies that such
an operation was planned, the end of TPS would still give federal agents — who
are operating under [mandatory arrest
quotas](https://www.axios.com/2025/12/04/trump-ice-immigration-arrests-
deportations) — an excuse to question any given Black person in Ohio under
suspicion that they may be an undocumented Haitian immigrant. After all,
President Trump’s [Supreme Court](https://eji.org/news/supreme-court-allows-
stops-based-on-race-to-continue/) justices have ruled that immigration
enforcement agents can use race as the basis for stopping people.

While the end of TPS for immigrants is particularly dangerous for people of
color, as the murders of [Renee Good](https://www.cnn.com/2026/01/08/us/renee-
nicole-good-minneapolis-ice-shooting-hnk) and [Alex
Pretti](https://www.propublica.org/article/alex-pretti-shooting-cbp-agents-
identified-jesus-ochoa-raymundo-gutierrez)make clear, more ICE is bad for
everyone.

What’s more, DHS is deporting them to nations — including
[Nicaragua](https://hrf.org/latest/nicaragua-escalates-political-repression-
remembering-peng-shuai/?gad_campaignid=1597499996),
[Honduras](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/why-is-honduras-
presidential-election-turmoil-weeks-after-voting-2025-12-19/), and
[Nepal](https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/02/04/nepal-protests-over-corruption-
inequality-and-social-media-ban) — that are currently facing political
turmoil.

The [Trump administration](https://forumtogether.org/article/temporary-
protected-status-fact-sheet/) has also terminated TPS for people from
Venezuela, Afghanistan, Cameroon, and Cuba. Since then, the U.S. has invaded
[Venezuela](https://www.wlrn.org/immigration/2026-01-09/venezuelan-tps-maduro-
deportation-democrats) and kidnapped President Nicolás Maduro. The Trump
administration is currently imposing a total blockade on oil imports to
[Cuba](https://truthout.org/articles/trumps-fuel-embargo-forces-cuba-to-take-
emergency-steps-to-avert-catastrophe/), while threatening retaliatory tariffs
on any country that sells oil to the Cuban government.
[Afghanistan](https://news.un.org/en/story/2025/12/1166684) and
[Cameroon](https://refugees.org/timeline-cameroon-the-anglophone-crisis/)
continue to struggle with their own political instability and social upheaval.

In short, none of these countries are in a position to welcome tens of
thousands of people.

At the same time that the Trump administration is deliberately manufacturing
these humanitarian crises, it is weakening international aid networks. This
includes eliminating the U.S. Agency for International Development
([USAID](https://www.oxfamamerica.org/explore/issues/making-foreign-aid-
work/what-do-trumps-proposed-foreign-aid-cuts-mean/)) and withdrawing the U.S.
from the [World Health
Organization](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cn9zznx8qdno), the [UN Human
Rights Council](https://www.politico.com/news/2025/02/03/us-withdraw-un-human-
rights-council-trump-00202100), and other organizations.

In their absence, vulnerable countries will be left to fend for themselves —
or worse, become the next victim of Trump’s global real estate firm: the
deceptively named [Board of
Peace](https://www.aljazeera.com/opinions/2026/1/25/gaza-is-not-a-real-estate-
fantasy).

[The Trump administration](https://forumtogether.org/article/temporary-
protected-status-fact-sheet/) has attempted and thus far been successfully
blocked from ending TPS for people from Ethiopia, Haiti, South Sudan, Burma,
and Syria. TPS is currently scheduled to end for Somali, Yemeni, Salvadoran,
Sudanese, and Ukrainian nationals in the upcoming months. While judges may
rule against some of these efforts, DHS will likely appeal until they find a
court that will give them the decision they want.

[TPS](https://www.rescue.org/article/behind-headlines-temporary-protected-
status) was specifically designed to aid those in need — its moral and
political duty cannot be forfeited to the racist and xenophobic whims of this
administration. We must stand with our immigrant neighbors and push our
elected officials to put guardrails on DHS’s clear abuse of power.

The post [Don’t End TPS for Our Immigrant
Neighbors](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/03/02/dont-end-tps-for-our-
immigrant-neighbors/) appeared first on
[CounterPunch.org](https://www.counterpunch.org).
